study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Sun et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2025
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dissecting heterogeneity in major depressive disorder via normative model-driven subtyping of functional brain networks

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed to develop normative models of network degree centrality as a function of age and sex for each brain region. The PCNtoolkit Python package version 0.28 was used for implementation. HBR allows for the imposition of a common prior distribution across multiple sites to estimate site-specific yet interrelated means and variances, thus accommodating signal and noise variability in multi-site data.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To minimize the impact of site-related variability on subsequent results, hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed in the HC cohort to develop a normative model of network degree centrality as a function of age and sex for each brain region. ... To implement normative modeling, we utilized the PCNtoolkit Python package, version 0.28
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Sun2025.pdf.md: Section 2.3 Capturing individual deviations from normative models

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The response variable was degree centrality (DC) of functional brain networks. Degree centrality was calculated for 96 brain regions defined by the Harvard-Oxford atlas. The area under the curve (AUC) of degree centrality across network sparsity thresholds ranging from 0.05 to 0.50 was used as the summarized scalar of network indicators. Degree centrality measures direct connections between network nodes and reflects the number of functional connections a brain region has with other regions.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: In this study, age and sex were mapped onto the degree centrality of brain functional networks. ... Degree centrality for each brain region was calculated at every sparsity threshold using the Graph Theoretical Network Analysis Toolbox (GRETNA), with the area under the curve (AUC) across all thresholds defined as a summarized scalar of network indicators.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Sun2025.pdf.md: Section 2.2 Brain network analysis; Section 2.3 Capturing individual deviations from normative models

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as fixed-effect explanatory variables mapped onto degree centrality. Site was incorporated as a hierarchical (random) effect in the HBR model to accommodate multi-site data variability while preserving meaningful site-related variations.
